C001.reason: Constructing a VehicleTelemetry message to send; the speed field is now int32 on the wire. Must quantize finite request['speed'] (float) to int32 meters per second with clamp and truncation toward zero before assignment.

C002.reason: Reading the decoded entity.speed_mps; after regeneration this is already an int value. The observation returns the integer speed as required, no source change needed.

C003.reason: Comparing decoded entity.speed_mps (now int) against float literal 30.0. Must change the threshold to integer 30 to match the intended strict >30 comparison on the integer wire value.

rationale: C001 quantizes the outgoing speed: finite floats are truncated toward zero via int(), then clamped to int32 range; non-finite values become 0. C003 changes the comparison from 30.0 to 30 so the strict >30 threshold applies to the decoded integer speed_mps. C002 simply reads the already-integer field and requires no change.
assumptions: request['speed'] is always a JSON number (float) per the existing contract.
Non-finite speed values are treated as 0 per typical quantization fallback.
The generated protobuf binding exposes speed_mps as a Python int after regeneration.
No other code paths construct VehicleTelemetry messages with speed_mps.
